title: The derived-limit counit recovers a compatible tower family from its cone lift
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be the category of modules on a small ringed site [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and let $C_\bullet=(C_m,t_m)$ be a strict inverse tower of complexes. Choose a K-injective tower resolution $q:C_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ whose terms $I^p_\bullet$ are injective objects of the category of strict towers [def-pur-kinjective-complex, def-sp-injective-resolutions, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], so that $R\lim C_\bullet=\lim I_\bullet$ [def-weil-derived-limit] and the inclusion $\iota:\lim I_\bullet\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1](I_\bullet)$, with zero shifted-product component, is a quasi-isomorphism. Let $\epsilon_C:\Delta R\lim C_\bullet\to C_\bullet$ be the derived-limit counit in the derived category of strict towers, namely $[q]^{-1}$ composed with the ordinary limit-cone map $\Delta\lim I_\bullet\to I_\bullet$. If $P$ is a complex and $\theta_m:P\to C_m$ is a compatible family, $t_m\circ\theta_{m+1}=\theta_m$, write $\theta^\Delta:\Delta P\to C_\bullet$ for the induced strict tower map and $\tilde\theta:P\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1](C_\bullet)$ for the cone lift $z\mapsto(0,(\theta_m(z))_m)$. Let $r_\theta=[\iota]^{-1}\circ[\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1](q)\circ\tilde\theta]:P\to R\lim C_\bullet$. Then in the derived category of strict towers
$$\epsilon_C\circ\Delta(r_\theta)=\theta^\Delta.$$
Thus the cone lift realizes the given compatible family at every level; the equality is before applying any further functor or passing to individual quotient derived categories, and no exactness of countable products is assumed.

proof.text: The nth degree-p component of the constant-complex map of b followed by lambdaMap is b.f p followed by the nth limit projection, by hlambdaMap. This equals (θ n).f p followed by (q.f p).app (op n), and hence equals the component of thetaDelta followed by q, by hthetaDelta. Extensionality of natural transformations and complex morphisms gives Δ(b) lambdaMap = thetaDelta q.

This proves exactly Q.map thetaDelta in the derived category of strict towers.
